records.real_world_identity_notes: The PMR observation resolves to the Marcos Mantara LM600 race-car family. PMR's N-GT label is simulator taxonomy; PMR's own history places the modeled context in the early 2000s and mentions a 2000 British GT1 win. Period records also show LM600s in LM GT2 and a 1999 FIA homologation, so the exact PMR chassis and year remain unpinned. The evidence supports six forward gears and includes a sequential six-speed race configuration, but it also documents a different homologated LM600 configuration with a ZF synchronized manual gearbox. No reviewed source establishes the exact shift interface, clutch technique, shift electronics, or original steering-wheel geometry for the PMR target.
records.confidence_basis: PMR's official car page names Marcos Mantara LM600 and lists a six-speed sequential transmission. Its dated history article places the modeled historical context in the early 2000s and specifically mentions a 2000 British GT1 result. The 1997 Le Mans record identifies an exact Mantara LM600 chassis with a Hewland sequential six-speed, while the FIA GT010 homologation form identifies the same model and documents a separate ZF six-speed manual/synchronized configuration. The repository contains no existing curated record for this identity, so a new record is proposed with the variant boundary made explicit.

records.specification_basis: PMR lists six speeds; the exact 1997 race record lists a Hewland six-speed; and the FIA homologation form provides six forward ratios. The sources agree on the count even though they document different gearbox configurations. Manual blip is a downshift action in this controls model; no upshift-blip claim is asserted. Automatic blip is a downshift action in this controls model; no upshift-blip claim is asserted. Throttle lift is represented as an upshift action in this controls model; no separate downshift-lift claim is asserted. Automatic cut is represented as an upshift action in this controls model; no downshift-cut claim is asserted. The reviewed sources did not establish the remaining technique and wheel fields, which stay unknown in the real-car baseline: /authentic_controls/transmission/shift_actuation, /authentic_controls/transmission/shift_pattern, /authentic_controls/transmission/standing_start_clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/throttle_lift, /authentic_controls/transmission/upshift/automatic_cut, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/clutch, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/manual_blip, /authentic_controls/transmission/downshift/automatic_blip, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shape, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/open_top, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/integrated_display, /authentic_controls/steering/wheel_rim/shift_lights.
